applicant_utility.summary: This is one of the more complete undergraduate packages at a Singapore university: subsidised tuition for up to four years after the Tuition Grant, S$6,000 a year paid as S$3,000 each term, a travel award of up to S$5,000 for an approved overseas programme, priority for SUTD's Global Education Exchange and Fifth Row leadership development, and no bond. It is only open to Singapore Citizens, and the critical mechanical point is that you apply for it inside the SUTD admission application - SUTD says there is no other way to apply, so you cannot bolt it on afterwards.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Singapore Citizens admitted or applying to SUTD undergraduate programmes who want tuition, a termly allowance and overseas mobility in one bond-free award
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm Singapore Citizenship, since the award is closed to everyone else
Elect to apply for the scholarship inside the SUTD admission application - this is the only route and it cannot be added later
Plan to take up the Tuition Grant Scheme, since the tuition subsidy depends on it; without the grant you would pay higher non-subsidised fees
Check that your chosen programme combination is not excluded, since SUTD warns that some scholarships do not consider programmes with DDP and SINGA options
Budget assuming S$3,000 per academic term, not S$6,000 in one payment
Keep your academic record strong, since the award is described as highly attractive and merit-based
common_rejection_risks: Submitting only the admission application and missing the in-application scholarship election, which is irreversible
Declining or missing the Tuition Grant Scheme, which removes the subsidised tuition basis of the award
Applying for a programme with DDP and SINGA options without checking whether this scholarship considers those combinations
Losing the award by exceeding the normal minimum duration, since the four-year tuition coverage is tied to that duration
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living and accommodation costs beyond the S$6,000 annual allowance, any overseas programme cost above the S$5,000 travel award, and any study beyond the normal minimum duration of the programme
document_audit: No separate scholarship document list is published, so the scholarship rides entirely on the admission application - make the evidence inside it complete and correct
Because selection criteria are not disclosed, do not rely on a specific portfolio or essay; prepare for a general merit assessment alongside the admissions process
alerts: SUTD publishes no selection criteria for this award, returning a no-info placeholder, so your best lever is a strong admissions application rather than a targeted scholarship strategy
The scholarship is bond-free but the tuition basis depends on taking the Tuition Grant Scheme
The S$5,000 travel award is for an approved overseas programme administered by the university and is separate from the priority consideration for GEXP, which remains subject to competition
SUTD warns on its scholarship pages that terms may change, so re-verify the value and conditions at the point of your own offer
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply for admission to SUTD and elect the scholarship in that same application, then accept the Tuition Grant Scheme and expect the allowance to be disbursed at S$3,000 per academic term

applicant_utility.summary: This is a family of small one-year NTU awards worth between S$3,000 and S$16,000, applied for with a single online application in a July window, and they are only available once you are already at NTU - current undergraduates, or freshmen two days after matriculation. Because they run on their own July cycle, they stay reachable even if you have missed the main Nanyang Scholarship window, and one application automatically covers the whole range. The AY2026-27 round closed on 31 July 2026 and NTU has not yet published AY2027-28 dates, so keep an eye on the scholarship page each June.
